counterexample: Line 0055's inequality is false: take T = path a-b-c (n=3), v_i = a. The component C of T-a containing b has |C| = 2 > n/2 = 1.5. The component of T - b containing a is {a}, of size 1 = n - |C|, not n - |C| - 1 = 0; and the asserted bound '< n/2 - 1 = 0.5' fails since 1 > 0.5.
reasoning_summary: 0001-0003 OK: announces induction on n = |V(T)|; a legitimate proof strategy. 0004-0007 OK: base cases n=1 (no components, vacuous) and n=2 (single component of size 1 <= 2/2 = 1) are both correct. 0008-0009 OK: strong inductive hypothesis for all trees with fewer than n vertices, n >= 3. 0010 OK: a tree with n >= 2 vertices has a leaf u. 0011-0012 OK: w is the unique neighbor of u; T' = T - u is a tree on n-1 vertices (deleting a leaf preserves treeness). 0012-0015 OK: applying the IH to T' yields v with every component of T'-v of size at most (n-1)/2. 0016 OK: case split on whether v = w. 0017-0019 OK: if v = w, the components of T - v are exactly {u} together with the components of T' - v (u's only neighbor was w = v). 0020-0021 OK: |{u}| = 1 <= n/2 since n >= 2. 0022-0025 OK: the remaining components have size <= (n-1)/2 <= n/2, so v works; Case 1 is complete and correct. 0026-0028 OK: if v != w, the components of T - v are the components of T' - v with u re-attached to the one containing w. 0029-0033 OK as arithmetic: that component can have size up to (n-1)/2 + 1 = (n+1)/2. 0034-0037 OBJECTION (soft): the inference is loose - (n+1)/2 > n/2 only shows the inductive bound is too weak to conclude, not that the condition 'would violate' anything; no actual violation is exhibited. 0038 FIRST FAILING STEP: the proof abandons Case 2 ('we must adjust our approach') without ever discharging it. Case 2 is left unproven, so the induction announced at 0002 is never completed, and nothing later closes it. 0039-0040 OK: the substitute algorithm starts at an arbitrary v0 and stops if v0 works. 0041-0043 OK: if v0 fails there is a component C of T - v0 with |C| > n/2, and v0 has a unique neighbor v1 in C (T is a tree, so exactly one edge joins v0 to C). 0044 OK: iterate. 0045-0048 UNJUSTIFIED: 'Since T is finite and we're moving toward larger components each time, the process must terminate' is not a termination argument - finiteness alone does not preclude revisiting vertices, and 'moving toward larger components each time' is both unproved and in direct contradiction with the monotone-decrease claim asserted at 0056. The needed fact (the offending component strictly shrinks, hence no vertex repeats) is never established. 0049-0053 OK: correct setup, and correct that the component of T-v_{i+1} containing v_i is the union of the other components of T-v_i together with v_i. 0054-0055 INCORRECT: that union has size n - |C|, not n - |C| - 1 (v_i plus the n-1-|C| vertices outside C give n - |C|), and the derived bound '< n/2 - 1' is false; the true and sufficient bound is n - |C| < n/2. Concrete failure: T = a-b-c, v_i = a, |C| = 2, backward component {a} has size 1, while the claimed value is 0 and the claimed bound 0.5. 0056-0057 UNJUSTIFIED: 'the process strictly reduces the maximum component size' does not follow from the preceding bullet, which bounds only the backward component containing v_i; the argument that any still-oversized component at v_{i+1} must sit strictly inside C (and hence be strictly smaller) is never given, so the key monotone quantity driving termination is missing. 0058 UNJUSTIFIED: 'Therefore, by induction' is a non-sequitur - the induction was abandoned at 0038 with Case 2 open, and the replacement argument is algorithmic rather than inductive, so this conclusion rests on neither a completed induction nor a completed algorithmic proof. The theorem itself is true (a tree centroid has this property), but this write-up does not prove it: the induction is left incomplete and the substitute argument contains a false inequality (0055) and an unproved termination/monotonicity claim (0045-0048, 0056).
